title: The religion is sincere counsel
cue: The religion is sincere counsel: to whom?
arabic: عَنْ أَبِي رُقَيَّةَ تَمِيمِ بْنِ أَوْسٍ الدَّارِيِّ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ ﷺ قَالَ: «الدِّينُ النَّصِيحَةُ». قُلْنَا: لِمَنْ؟ قَالَ: «لِلَّهِ، وَلِكِتَابِهِ، وَلِرَسُولِهِ، وَلِأَئِمَّةِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ وَعَامَّتِهِمْ».
translation: It is narrated from Abu Ruqayyah Tamim ibn Aws al-Dari, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “The religion is sincere counsel.” We said: “To whom?” He said: “To Allah, to His Book, to His Messenger, to the leaders of the Muslims and to their common people.”

witnesses.name: ibn-daqiq-sharh
witnesses.ref: Ibn Daqiq al-'Id, Sharh al-Arba'in, Mu'assasat al-Rayyan 2003, hadith 7, p. 50: https://shamela.ws/book/11244/40

witnesses.name: haytami-fath-al-mubin
witnesses.ref: al-Haytami, al-Fath al-Mubin, Dar al-Minhaj 2008, hadith 7, p. 253: https://shamela.ws/book/8889/249

provenance.note: Hashes are of each witness's text of this narration, from al-Nawawi's opening words to the end before his attribution line, with honorific formulas written as we print them (ﷺ, رضي الله عنه): see data-sources/hadith-arabic/SOURCE.md. All three witnesses agree with ours.

notes.text: Ibn Daqiq al-'Id says "sincere counsel" is a word that gathers in wanting every good for the one counselled; no other single Arabic word says all of it.

source.work: Ibn Daqiq al-'Id, Sharh al-Arba'in al-Nawawiyya
